- **Precise latest source investigation, NO older measurements rerun**: exact original [GLib 2.82.4 gwin32appinfo.c](https://github.com/GNOME/glib/blob/2.82.4/gio/gwin32appinfo.c) and [gwin32packageparser.c](https://github.com/GNOME/glib/blob/2.82.4/gio/gwin32packageparser.c) were inspected. `update_registry_data()` destroys/recreates **six** owned roots (`apps_by_id`, `apps_by_exe`, `fake_apps`, `urls`, `extensions`, `handlers`) before scanning; a per-scan `uwp_handler_table` is unref'd after parser use; per-package parser cleanup releases **five HSTRINGs** and **10 COM interface** kinds (per-item plus global), and XML parse cleanup releases five SAX-owned state members and XML COM/stream refs. The already-applied experimental [weak-backref patch](https://github.com/taku077/c545d-recorder/blob/main/tests/patch_glib_appinfo_weak_backrefs.py) was applied to a **temporary copy** of original `gwin32appinfo.c` and its `GWeakRef` init/set/get/clear, finalization and original public `GAppInfo` strong-ref ownership cross-checked. These are **source-order/resource-release contract facts**, NOT proof of no surviving owners, native buffers, or memory leaks.
- **New distinct source defect candidate, outside successful-registry-scan leak attribution**: original `g_win32_package_parser_enum_packages()` uses `CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED)` and can `goto cleanup` when that call fails (or even before initialization on DLL API errors), but calls `CoUninitialize()` unconditionally in the cleanup tail. Microsoft's [CoInitializeEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/combaseapi/nf-combaseapi-coinitializeex) and [CoUninitialize](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/combaseapi/nf-combaseapi-couninitialize) guidance requires one uninitialize only for a *successful* init (including `S_FALSE`); an STA request on an MTA thread may fail with `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE`. **This is a code-level failure-path imbalance risk**, **NOT** an identified cause of observed normal-operation `PrivateUsage +368,640 B` or 360B bin counts.
